name: Backhand flick
summary: Attack a short ball with the backhand over the table. The banana flick adds sidespin.
whenToUse: Against short serves and pushes to your backhand or the middle. At level 4 and up, the banana flick can be used even against heavier backspin.

keyPoints.stance: Step in with your right foot (left foot if left-handed) so the ball is in front of you.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Lean over the table; chest stays over the ball.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Short: the wrist does most of the work.
keyPoints.timing: At the top of the bounce.
keyPoints.batArm: Elbow high and forward. Wrist cocks back with the bat tip pointing toward you, then flicks out.
keyPoints.recovery: Step back to ready at once.
keyPoints.anticipation: Against backspin brush up the back of the ball; for a banana flick, brush around the side.

learningPath.task: Watch the wrist cock back, then flick out.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along: step in, cock, flick, step out.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Was the elbow up and forward?
Did the wrist cock back first?

learningPath.task: Flick short no-spin balls to the backhand.
Drop short or flick, depending on the ball.

gamePatterns.situation: A short serve to your middle or backhand.
gamePatterns.how: Backhand flick to their wide forehand or elbow, then expect a block.

fixes: Open the face and brush up
Close the face against light spin

penholdNotes: With penhold, use the reverse side for the backhand flick.
